headline: Altcoins surge as NEAR jumps 16% and Google's quantum breakthrough rattles Bitcoin security debate
summary: A broad altcoin rally stole the show Friday, with NEAR Protocol and Celestia each climbing over 16% as Bitcoin steadied above $82,000 and traders rotated into layer-1 alternatives. Google's latest quantum computing milestone added an unexpected dimension to the day — experts flagged that 6.4 million Bitcoin in early wallets could eventually be at risk, prompting Starknet to open a governance vote on restructuring its architecture. The rest of this report covers the MSCI index shake-up threatening Strategy and Metaplanet, and Circle's push into 40 new markets.

winners.name: NEAR Protocol
winners.catalyst: NEAR surged 16.21% as Bitcoin's stabilization above $82,000 fueled a broad rotation into layer-1 altcoins — Celestia's simultaneous 16% jump suggests sector-wide momentum rather than a NEAR-specific catalyst.

losers.name: Bitway
losers.catalyst: No clear catalyst identified; Bitway fell 6.60% against the broader market's upward trend, suggesting idiosyncratic selling pressure.

whyItMoved: Bitcoin's consolidation above $82,000 gave traders the confidence to reach further out the risk curve. With BTC up a relatively modest 1.58%, the real action was in layer-1 altcoins: NEAR Protocol jumped 16.21%, Celestia gained 16%, Solana rose 4.45%, Ethereum climbed 4.27%, and Chainlink added 5.24%. Zcash was a notable outlier, surging 14.08% — privacy coins also benefited from the day's quantum computing headlines, as Google's latest milestone renewed interest in cryptographic security. The Federal Reserve angle added a layer of macro uncertainty: Fed Chair candidate Kevin Warsh declined to signal any direction on interest rates, leaving traders without a clear read on monetary policy. That ambiguity didn't derail the rally, but it kept Bitcoin's gains contained while altcoins ran. The rotation pattern — Bitcoin stable, altcoins outperforming — is a familiar one when sentiment recovers from a dip and traders seek higher-beta exposure. Fear & Greed held at 63 (Greed), consistent with a market that is optimistic but not euphoric.
worthKnowing: Google's quantum computing breakthrough reignited debate over Bitcoin's long-term security — experts estimate 6.4 million BTC in early-format wallets could eventually be vulnerable, and Starknet opened a governance vote on restructuring as an independent layer-1 to address the threat.

MSCI finalized new index rules that could remove crypto treasury companies — including Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) and Japan's Metaplanet — from major equity indexes, which would reduce the indirect Bitcoin exposure available to traditional fund managers.
A federal judge rejected a joint Gemini-CFTC bid to unwind a $5 million settlement, affirming that regulatory enforcement outcomes hold even when both parties later seek to reverse them.
Circle announced plans to expand USDC into 40 new international markets, accelerating its push to compete with Tether for global stablecoin dominance.
